title: Billing Sandbox: Entitlement Shadowing & Safe Overage Simulation
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Finance and Sales need a low-risk way to validate how plan changes (trial->paid, seat adds, plan migrations) and routing fallbacks affect invoices before they hit customers. Current practice requires provisioning test tenants or manual spreadsheet simulations that diverge from production behaviors (rate-limit enforcement, per-model weights, cross-plan crediting).

Objective: Build a Billing Sandbox feature (entitlement shadowing) that mirrors production metering and enforcement logic for a subset of accounts and produces deterministic invoice projections, simulated overage events, and a replayable audit trail without affecting live entitlements or charging. The sandbox should support: trial cohorts, sales-run forecasts, and internal QA acceptance testing for pricing changes and emergency rollouts.

Deliverables: PRD describing data flows, a feature toggle to enable entitlements shadowing for selected orgs, replay engine for X days of historical requests, simulated invoice artifact (PDF/CSV) and a dashboard with diff view vs. real billing, and acceptance tests for common migration/overage scenarios.
acceptance_criteria: Given a sandbox-enabled account when a plan migration is executed the sandbox must produce a simulated invoice that includes prorated credits and calculates overage as per current rate table without modifying live billing ledgers

When a ramped traffic trace is replayed into the sandbox the system must apply the same per-route rate limits, per-model token weights, and prioritized entitlement fallbacks as production and emit a timeline of throttles and overage events
Sandbox projections must be reproducible: running the same historical trace twice (with same config) yields identical simulated invoices and event timelines
Sales and Finance users can request a CSV export and a PDF summary of the simulated invoice for a specified date window (max 90 days) and receive it within 2 minutes for traces under 10M tokens
No sandbox run shall write to production charge ledgers, quota counters, or mutate customer entitlements; any side effects must be gated behind a distinct simulation namespace

A diff view must show line-by-line differences between simulated and actual billing for the same timeframe, highlighting root causes (proration, overage, model-weight mismatch, rate limit conversions)
End-to-end automated tests covering trial->paid migration, per-route fallback to cheaper model, and cross-env credit reconciliation pass in CI and are green for release
Telemetry: simulation runs emit metrics (run_count, duration_ms, token_count, discrepancy_tokens, discrepancy_cost_usd) to the billing observability pipeline
scope: In-scope: entitlement shadowing for hosted accounts and dedicated customers with online metering. UI controls in Console to enable sandbox per-org, CSV/PDF exports, replay engine for bounded historical windows, simulation namespace for all metering events, and backend adapters that reuse production rating tables. Out-of-scope: automated chargeable corrections, external invoicing system writes, and private on-prem package at launch.
non_goals: Do not implement billing automation (e.g. automatic refunds), do not allow sandbox runs to modify billing ledgers or quota enforcement in production, and do not support on-prem/offline deployments for first release.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature flag rollout to internal orgs and Finance (flag OFF by default). 2) Pilot with 3 Sales accounts and Finance team for two weeks. 3) Broaden to QA and Solutions Engineers. 4) Open beta to customers by opt-in. 5) GA after two successful pilots and resolution of top 5 discrepancy sources.
open_questions: Should sandbox use a time-shifted view of quotas or a separate independent quota namespace?
What SLA for simulation latency is acceptable for files >50M tokens?
Do we need to simulate currency conversion fees in MVP or defer to later?
notes: Trade-offs discussed: a full double-write (writing to production ledgers) gives highest fidelity but is unacceptable for safety; we choose simulation namespace to eliminate real charges. Scope chosen to maximize coverage for hosted customers where most early billing disputes originate. Implementing model-weight parity required a small upstream change to rating tables (dependency ENG-21500).
